source:
Tara: I am not trying to kill the appointment reminder project. We agree reminder texts reduce no-shows and that patients need an easy opt-out. I just think texts should be the default unless someone declines.
Luis: Yes, nobody is arguing against reminders or opt-outs. I object to making texts the default because some patients share phones and may not want clinic messages appearing there.
Tara: Then put the opt-out in the intake form and every message. If we ask people to opt in first, the no-show problem stays exactly where it is.
Luis: I can live with reminders. I want consent before the first message, not after.

extraction.mainQuestion: Should clinic reminder texts be default-on or opt-in?

positions.label: Default-on reminders
positions.thesis: Appointment reminder texts should be on by default with an easy opt-out.
positions.steelman: Default-on reminders preserve the no-show benefit while still giving patients a way to decline.

groundingQuotes.quote: texts should be the default unless someone declines.

positions.label: Consent before first text
positions.thesis: Reminder texts should require consent before the first message.
positions.steelman: Patients who share phones should not receive clinic messages unless they first agree.

groundingQuotes.quote: I want consent before the first message, not after.

claims.statement: Requiring opt-in would preserve too much of the no-show problem.

resolution.condition: The clinic must decide whether participation defaults or first-message consent should govern rollout.

groundingQuotes.quote: If we ask people to opt in first, the no-show problem stays exactly where it is.

claims.statement: Shared-phone privacy makes first-message consent necessary.

resolution.condition: The clinic must decide how privacy consent should be obtained.

groundingQuotes.quote: some patients share phones and may not want clinic messages appearing there.

commonGroundCandidates.statement: Both participants support reminder texts as a no-show intervention.

groundingQuotes.quote: We agree reminder texts reduce no-shows

commonGroundCandidates.statement: Both participants accept that patients need an opt-out.

groundingQuotes.quote: nobody is arguing against reminders or opt-outs.

disagreementCandidates.question: Should consent be handled by default-on opt-out or by opt-in before the first message?
disagreementCandidates.summary: They mostly agree on reminders and opt-outs, but disagree about the consent default.
disagreementCandidates.resolutionCondition: Choose the consent procedure for the reminder rollout.

caveats: The disagreement is narrow relative to the amount of shared ground in the exchange.
